newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: PRESS DIGEST - Czech Republic - Jan 29.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Czech Republic - Jan 29.

text.p: MLADA FRONTA DNES - The Health Ministry responded to warnings from large hospitals that due to debts, they cannot provide proper care to their patients, by announcing that two Prague hospitals - General Faculty Hospital and Faculty Hospital Motol - are in serious need of help. For the directors of the hospitals, this announcement means a severe reduction in power.

- Only two Czech corporations have a good chance of entering the tender for obtaining shares of the largest munitions factory in the country Aero Vodochody. Czech Airlines, which has joined with Boeing, and Chemopol Group, who is connected with another American firm Lockheed Martin are still in the running, while Cimex Holding, the third Czech company competing for ownership, is according to experts, out of the tender.

LIDOVE NOVINY - Reports from experts as to how many schools participated in the first day of chain strikes in four districts vary. The director of the Education Administration in Nachod stated that 37 schools were closed in his district, while union members said 70 were closed. Both the Administration and unions agree that over 120 schools are on strike in Brno.

HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - In the past few days, Chemapol Group completed its final wave of issuing shares, and in so doing increased its basic capital to more than 2.5 billion crowns. Many banking, financial, industrial and trade institutions showed interest in buying the 826,404 shares at a nominal value of 1,000 crowns each.

- McDonnell Douglas announced yesterday that it is offering to loan the Czech Republic seven F/A-18 Hornets for five years for no charge. Czech pilots would begin training to fly in six months and the air force will be permitted to fly the Hornets 18 months after the signing of the contract.

- After yesterday, the Engineering Federation is prepared to strike. They are not happy with a 15 percent salary increase which they received at the beginning of the year and request a further increase of 1.2 percent.

PRAVO - On Monday and Tuesday, Chairman of Parliament and the Social Democrats (CSSD), Milos Zeman, presented German President Roman Herzog and German officials in Bonn with three variations on his idea for an accompanying document to the Czech-German Declaration. Foreign politics expert and representative of the German Social Democratic Party (SPD), Karsten Voigt, commented that all three proposals are reasonable.
